svg.title: The bakery owner's six requests matched to AWS services
svg.desc: Six cards in two columns. 1, sales dashboard: in, sales files in S3 queried with Athena; out, charts the owner can read; service, Amazon Quick Sight; not Athena alone, which answers queries but draws no charts. 2, phone bot: in, a caller's voice; out, a conversation that understands the request; service, Amazon Lex on a phone line from Amazon Connect Customer; not Polly alone, which speaks but doesn't understand. 3, spoken product descriptions: in, written text; out, lifelike speech; service, Amazon Polly; not Transcribe, which turns speech into text. 4, receipts turned into text: in, photos of paper receipts; out, text and fields such as supplier, date and total; service, Amazon Textract; not Rekognition, which finds text in images but not document fields. 5, desktops for seasonal staff: in, staff on their own devices; out, a whole desktop streamed to them; service, Amazon WorkSpaces; not buying PCs, and if staff need one app only, WorkSpaces Applications. 6, freezer sensors: in, temperature readings from devices; out, readings in AWS and an alert; service, AWS IoT Core; not Kinesis alone, which streams data but doesn't connect and manage devices. Names as of 2026-10-24: Quick Sight was QuickSight, Connect Customer was Amazon Connect, WorkSpaces Applications was AppStream 2.0.
